title: Finite Tor amplitude and perfectness over the finite coefficient ring
statement:
Let $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ be the
finite coefficient ring,
so that $A$ is a local Artinian ring with maximal ideal
$(\varpi_E)$, and let $C$ be a bounded complex of $A$-modules
whose cohomology modules are finite, i.e. an object of the
finite-coefficient
category over a point of the trace-formula chapter. Then $C$ has
finite Tor amplitude if and
only if $C$ lies in $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ in the sense of
[def-trf-categorical-trace], i.e. if and only if $C$ is
quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated free
$A$-modules.
Here finite Tor amplitude is the ordinary-module condition: there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^i(C\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}M)=0$ for every $A$-module $M$ placed in degree zero and every $i\notin[a,b]$. The notation $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ in the conclusion refers specifically to the perfect category of [def-trf-categorical-trace], rather than to the category of all bounded complexes with finite cohomology.

note: *Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

proof.text: Put R = A_{E,n}. Its finiteness follows from [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]; hence IsNoetherianRing R follows by isNoetherian_of_finite, giving [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Obtain the local integer ring, maximal ideal m, and equality span {uniformizer} = m from [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] at the recorded spectral absolute value. Since n >= 1, m^n <= m and m is proper. Thus the coefficient ideal is proper and R is nontrivial. IsLocalRing.of_surjective' applied to the quotient map makes R local. Boundedness of C supplies an upper cohomology bound, and hfinite is exactly finite generation [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

Apply the reverse direction of [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-pseudocoherent-cohomology-criterion] to R and C. The upper homology bound comes from the bounded t-structure hypothesis using isZero_of_isLE, while hfinite supplies every finite cohomology module. This proves IsPseudoCoherent C, the shared predicate of [def-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-complex]. No assumptions on the terms of a representative are introduced.

Given finite Tor amplitude, apply [lem-pc-ring-pseudo-coherent-finite-tor-perfect] to C and the pseudo-coherence just proved. Unpack its bounded finite-projective representative P. Convert the pointwise support condition to P.IsStrictlyGE and P.IsStrictlyLE using their iff lemmas, reverse Q(P) ≅ C, and package the result as IsPerfectRingComplex C [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex], the perfect-category condition of [def-trf-categorical-trace].

Unpack any perfect representative P. Each term is flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat] and finite free over the local ring by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-flat-local-free]. Keep exactly P and its differentials: the requested representative only asks for Module.Free and Module.Finite, not a chosen identification with R^r. Conversely free terms are projective by [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], so the same representative packages as perfect.

For the reverse finite-Tor implication, use a perfect representative P supported between a and b. Its projective terms are flat by [lem-weil-pbc-projective-module-flat]; ModuleCat.flat_iff_flat converts this to categorical flatness. Apply [lem-trf-source-bounded-flat-tor-amplitude], namely the existing proved generic torAmplitudeIn_Q_obj_of_flat, to get Tor amplitude [a,b] for Q(P). Transport along Q(P) ≅ C and widen the interval to [min a b,b], which is ordered even when the original support interval was empty. Combine with the previous implications to prove both displayed equivalences unchanged.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ be the
finite coefficient ring,
so that $A$ is a local Artinian ring with maximal ideal
$(\varpi_E)$, and let $C$ be a bounded complex of $A$-modules
whose cohomology modules are finite, i.e. an object of the
finite-coefficient
category over a point. Then $C$ has
finite Tor amplitude if and
only if $C$ lies in $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ in the sense of
[def-trf-categorical-trace], i.e. if and only if $C$ is
quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of finitely generated free
$A$-modules.

proof.text:
Write $A=A_{E,n}$ for the finite coefficient ring of
[def-trf-coefficient-conventions]: it is a local ring with
maximal ideal $(\varpi_E)$.

*(If.)* Suppose that $C$ is quasi-isomorphic to a bounded
complex $P^\bullet$ of finite free $A$-modules with $P^i=0$ for
$i\notin[a,b]$. For every $A$-module $M$ the derived tensor
$C\otimes_A^LM\cong P^\bullet\otimes_AM$ is concentrated in degrees
$[a,b]$, so that $\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(C,M)=0$ for
$i\notin[a,b]$: in the notation of
[def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude] the complex $C$ has finite Tor
amplitude, and it is perfect in the sense of
[def-trf-categorical-trace] by construction.

*(Only if.)* Suppose that $C$ has finite Tor amplitude, i.e. finite tor dimension in the sense of
[Stacks, Tag 0652](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0652)
(Definition 15.68.1, in Section 15.68, Tor dimension).
Each cohomology module $H^i(C)$ is finite by hypothesis, hence
$0$-pseudo-coherent as an $A$-module by
[Stacks, Tag 064T](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/064T);
since $C$ is bounded it lies in $D^-(A)$, so
[Stacks, Tag 066B](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/066B)
shows that the complex $C$ itself is pseudo-coherent. By
[Stacks, Tag 0658](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0658) a
pseudo-coherent complex of finite tor dimension over a ring is
perfect, and if it has tor amplitude in $[a,b]$ it is
quasi-isomorphic to a complex $E^\bullet$ of finite projective
$A$-modules with $E^i=0$ for $i\notin[a,b]$. Since $A$ is a
local ring, a finite projective $A$-module is free
([Stacks, Tag 00NZ](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00NZ),
Lemma 10.78.5: a finite flat module over a local ring is finite free;
equivalently
[Tag 00NX](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00NX), Lemma 10.78.2,
parts (2) and (5), together with Nakayama's lemma), so that
$E^\bullet$ is a bounded
complex of finitely generated free $A$-modules quasi-isomorphic to
$C$: $C$ lies in the category $D^b_{\mathrm{fin}}(A)$ of
[def-trf-categorical-trace].

The finite-Tor-amplitude hypothesis cannot be dropped in the second
direction: the module $A/(\varpi_E)$, viewed as a complex
concentrated in degree $0$, has finite cohomology modules, while its
minimal free resolution

$$
\cdots\to A\xrightarrow{\varpi_E}A\xrightarrow{\varpi_E}A\to
A/(\varpi_E)\to0
$$

is infinite, so that $\operatorname{Tor}_i^A(A/(\varpi_E), A/(\varpi_E))\cong A/(\varpi_E)\neq0$ for all $i\geq0$ and
$A/(\varpi_E)$ is not quasi-isomorphic to a bounded complex of
finite free $A$-modules.
